sentences.text: Philosophy of mathematics asks what numbers, sets, structures, and proofs are and how mathematical knowledge is possible.
The apparent necessity and abstractness of mathematical truths create problems for theories of knowledge based exclusively on sensory observation.
Gottlob Frege and Bertrand Russell sought logical foundations for mathematics.
David Hilbert developed a programme centered on formal systems and consistency proofs.
L. E. J. Brouwer's intuitionism connects mathematics with constructive mental activity and questions some classical proof principles.
Kurt Gödel's incompleteness results placed limits on certain formalist ambitions.
Mathematical platonists treat mathematical objects as mind-independent.
Nominalists seek to avoid such commitments, while structuralists describe mathematical objects through positions and relations within patterns.
Paul Benacerraf's challenges concern both how abstract objects could be known and how numbers should be identified.
Set theory studies infinite collections and the axioms governing them.
Questions about the continuum hypothesis and large cardinals raise issues about independence, truth, and the justification of axioms.
Category theory offers a different language for relationships and structures, though its role as a foundation remains contested.
Mathematical knowledge depends on proof, but philosophers examine the roles of diagrams, examples, intuition, explanation, and computer verification.
Formal proof assistants and computer-assisted proofs invite questions about trust, surveyability, and the social organization of mathematical expertise.

Ancient Greek mathematical argument, Indian work on numeration and algebra, Chinese mathematical problem-solving, and mathematical traditions in the Islamic world developed varied techniques and standards of demonstration.
These histories complicate the idea that mathematics has one uninterrupted methodological origin or a single timeless style of proof.
Why does mathematics apply so effectively to the physical world?
Does mathematical explanation in science support realism about abstract entities?
Philosophers also examine probability, mathematical beauty, the epistemology of diagrams, and the relationships among logic, computation, and mathematical understanding.

Philosophy of mathematics asks what mathematical objects are and how we can know about them, given that numbers and sets seem not to be physical and mathematical knowledge seems to come from proof alone.

sentences.text: Logicism, from Frege and Russell, sought to reduce mathematics to logic; Frege's system fell to Russell's paradox, though a neo-logicism built on Hume's principle has been revived.

claims.excerpt: Russell showed that Frege's Basic Law V entails a contradiction.

sentences.text: Intuitionism, from Brouwer, treats mathematics as mental construction, rejects completed infinities and proofs of existence that give no construction, and so revises classical logic.

claims.excerpt: According to intuitionism, mathematics is essentially an activity of construction.

sentences.text: Formalism, from Hilbert, treated higher mathematics as a formal system whose consistency was to be proved; Gödel's incompleteness theorems undermined that hope.

claims.excerpt: Together, they entail that Hilbert's program fails.

sentences.text: Platonists hold that mathematical objects exist independently of us.
Gödel defended this view, and Quine and Putnam argued that, because our best scientific theories cannot do without mathematics, we are committed to the entities it describes.

Paul Benacerraf posed two problems for platonism: how we could know about abstract objects that we cannot causally interact with, and which sets the natural numbers really are, when several set-theoretic constructions serve equally well.

claims.excerpt: Benacerraf formulated an epistemological problem for a variety of platonistic positions.

sentences.text: Structuralists such as Shapiro and Resnik answer that mathematics describes structures, positions in patterns, and nominalists, such as Hartry Field, try to do without abstract objects altogether, or treat mathematics as a kind of useful fiction.
